title: Over 1,000 untainted 2016-panel school staff miss new cut-off; age bar may shut them out
dek: Clerks and Group D workers whose jobs were cancelled with the tainted 2016 panel failed to make the interview list in the fresh recruitment, and many are now too old to try again, reports say.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
More than 1,000 school clerks and Group D staff whose jobs were cancelled with the rest of the 2016 recruitment panel, though they were never accused of wrongdoing, have failed to make the interview list in the fresh recruitment held to replace them, according to reports, and many are now too old to sit the test again.

The West Bengal School Service Commission (WBSSC) put up the results of the written test for 2,989 clerk (Group C) and 5,488 Group D posts in state-aided schools on Thursday, 5 November, with region-wise cut-off marks. For general-category candidates the cut-off was 68 marks for clerks (67 for women) and 40 for Group D (39 for women) in most regions, the published tables show. Reports said the 2016-panel staff who missed out are now over the upper age limit, so the commission's next recruitment will be closed to them.

## Who has been left out

The affected staff were among the non-teaching employees appointed through the 2016 State Level Selection Test. In April 2025 the Supreme Court cancelled that entire panel, voiding about 25,753 teaching and non-teaching appointments, because the commission could not separate those who had been hired fairly from those who had obtained jobs through irregularities. It ordered a fresh selection process. The commission later published a list of 3,512 non-teaching staff, 1,163 in Group C and 2,349 in Group D, whom it identified as "tainted"; they were barred from the new process.

The rest, often described as "untainted" or "qualified" staff, were allowed to take the new test. Unlike untainted teachers, who were allowed by the court to keep working until the fresh recruitment was completed, the non-teaching staff were out of work, and one report said they had not been paid for the two years they were unable to go to school.

The written tests were held on 1 March 2026 for clerks and 8 March for Group D. Reports said the results were held up by the Assembly elections. Marks for work experience were taken into account, as in the teachers' recruitment, according to reports, but cut-offs were high in every zone.

## What they are saying

"We went to the new government again and again," one of the staff who lost their job told reporters, saying they had asked for arrangements to be made for qualified staff and that this had not been done. He said perhaps only 5 to 10 per cent of the qualified staff would end up with jobs. A teacher who has followed the case called the outcome "very unfortunate" and said the government should do something for those who did not clear the cut-off.

No comment from the commission or the state's school education department had been reported by Friday evening. The figure of more than 1,000 comes from reports and has not been confirmed by the commission.

## Why it matters

The 2016 recruitment scandal has been one of the most contested issues in Bengal politics for a decade, through investigations by the Central Bureau of Investigation, orders of the Calcutta High Court and the Supreme Court's 2025 judgment. The government that took office after this year's Assembly elections has promised large-scale recruitment, including 7,200 permanent panchayat posts announced this week. For the non-teaching staff who were cleared of wrongdoing but have now missed out, the age limit means the fresh process may have been their last chance at a government school job.

## What happens next

Being called for interview is not an offer of a job. The commission has not yet announced dates for document verification and interviews for the candidates who made the list. Those left out have said they will keep asking the state government to make arrangements for them.
